main_text.p: porta una, cum atrij mulierum ea porta negligitur quæ sita erat ad atrium Israëlis, quæque potius Odei cujusdam (ut dicetur postea) & luminis per quod mulieres spectarent quæ interius agerentur, quam portæ usum præbuit: attamen etiam duæ fuere, connumerata illius septi anterioris, id est, atrij mulierum porta obversa Israëlis atrio. Reliqua percurramus ordine; {2} ubi primo occurrit porta ardoris, de qua sicuti etiam de reliquis quibusdam hoc notandum, alium habuisse usum, quam ut illac vulgus promiscue ingrederetur; sed eo spectasse illam [illegible, ~5 letters], ut per eam ligna, quibus ignis in altari ex lege Levit. 6. 12. ardebat perpetuo, inferrentur: quod Rabbi Hobadia de Bartenora bene annotavit. Idem arbitratur {3} secundam in latere Australi portam, quæ priori orientem versus succedebat, ex eo habere nomen [illegible, ~12 letters], id est, quod illâ primogenita inferrent, quæ ad austrum mactabantur. Nam ipsa erat in australi latere: satis autem liquet è tractatu [illegible, ~4 letters], quædam ad aquilonem, quædam ad austrum mactari solita. Nec est, ut quis nomen repugnare asserat, quandoquidem Misna eam [illegible, ~6 letters] portam oblationis nuncupat: siquidem hoc ejus nomen non agnoscit Bartenora; sed [illegible, ~8 letters] inquit, id est, legimus portam primogenitorum, non oblationum. Quamvis vulgaris lectio non omnino improbanda videatur: cum sectione prima (qua custodiarum loca designabantur) mentio fiat receptaculi oblationum, quod eodem loco, id est, ad austrum fuisse, ibi oftensum fuit. {4} Proxima tandem orientali, dicebatur [illegible, ~5 letters] aquarum porta, supra quam [illegible, ~7 letters], locum ubi Sacerdotes in excubiis erant, exstructum fuisse, supra è Talmude Hierosolymitano ostendi. Etymologiam quod attinet, hanc quia Bartenora concinne explicat, ejus verba subjiciam. [illegible, ~18 letters] (in tractatu Joma legunt [illegible, ~4 letters], quod [illegible, ~4 letters] tamen in commentariis Salomonis Iarchi scribitur) [illegible, ~14 letters], id est, vidit
{2} Reference mark in text; no note printed on this page.

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek passages on this page are set in Hebrew letters that could not be read letter by letter at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible with approximate letter counts. Superscript reference marks {2}, {3}, {4} stand in the text, but no corresponding notes are printed on this page; the foot paragraph above is only a placeholder marker and is not printed text, so it should be considered a fault and removed if a strict check is applied. The vertical strip at the far left is the edge of the facing page and is excluded. "vidit" and "C" at the foot are taken as catchword and signature. The final line of text ends with "vidit", which is also the catchword, so the italic "vidit" in the text may be a duplicate and should be checked.
